title: Italian Grand Prix: Next Formula 1 Round in Monza
seoTitle: Italian Grand Prix: Next F1 Round in Monza
subtitle: After Lando Norris's win in the Netherlands, the series heads to the traditional Italian circuit for the 13th round of 2026.
excerpt: Formula 1 gears up for the Italian Grand Prix, the 13th round of the 2026 season, taking place at the Monza circuit.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Formula 1 is preparing for one of its most classic and anticipated venues: the Italian Grand Prix. The race, which will be the 13th round of the 2026 season, takes place in the first week of September, from the 4th to the 6th, at the Monza Autodrome, a week after Lando Norris's victory at the Dutch GP.

Formula 1 Prepares for Monza

After the showdown in Zandvoort, the Netherlands, the series takes a short break and lands at the National Autodrome of Monza. This circuit is one of the most traditional in Formula 1, hosting virtually every Italian race in the championship, with the sole exception being the 1980 Italian GP held in Imola.

Italy, together with Great Britain, are the only countries to have hosted Formula 1 races in all 76 seasons of the sport. Expectations are high for another thrilling race on this historic stage.

The Temple of Speed and Its History

Known as the “Temple of Speed,” the National Autodrome of Monza has welcomed Formula 1 since 1950. Its features include long straights and fast corners that demand minimal aerodynamic drag, delivering ultra‑high‑speed racing.

The track is an icon on the Formula 1 calendar, and its history is marked by memorable moments and fierce battles. Free practice and qualifying will take place on Friday and Saturday respectively, while Sunday is reserved for the main race.

Brazilian Drivers and the GP's Top Winners

In the history of the Italian Grand Prix, two names stand out as the biggest winners: Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher, both with five triumphs. Hamilton, who races with the support of the tifosi, the passionate Ferrari fans, has a chance to cement his record at Monza.

Brazil also boasts a successful legacy at this circuit. Nelson Piquet leads the list of Brazilian winners with four victories, followed by Rubens Barrichello with three wins. Ayrton Senna won twice, and Emerson Fittipaldi topped the podium once.

The Championship and Recent Controversy

The last winner of the Italian GP was Max Verstappen, last year. In the current 2026 championship, Kimi Antonelli arrives for his home race with a sizable lead, holding 59 points more than Lewis Hamilton. Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto sits 14th, ten points behind.

The 2025 edition of the Italian GP was marked by an impasse within McLaren. Lando Norris, who finished second, encountered a pit‑stop problem on lap 46 and was overtaken by teammate Oscar Piastri. To rectify the loss, the team intervened and ordered Piastri to give the position back to the Briton, securing second place for Norris and third for the Australian. Max Verstappen capitalised on the situation to win the race comfortably.

Where and When to Watch

The full program of the Italian Grand Prix will be broadcast on several channels. TV Globo will air the Sunday race, continuing the coverage of European races on free‑to‑air TV. Sportv3, Globoplay and F1TV Pro will show the complete schedule, including free practice, qualifying and the Monza race.

  • Friday, September 4:
  • Free Practice 1 – 7:30 a.m. (Brasília time)
  • Free Practice 2 – 11:00 a.m. (Brasília time)
  • Saturday, September 5:
  • Free Practice 3 – 7:30 a.m. (Brasília time)
  • Qualifying – 11:00 a.m. (Brasília time)

The ge.globo portal will also follow all activities in real time.
